steps.label: Firmware
steps.title: Install the firmware
steps.text: A new controller usually has no firmware, or not the one you want. Pick PX4 or ArduPilot below and flash it over the USB cable. If it already runs the firmware you want, continue.

steps.label: Aircraft
steps.title: Choose the aircraft type
steps.text: Tell the controller what it is flying. This decides which controllers run and how many motors it expects.

steps.label: Frame and motors
steps.title: Frame, motors and positions
steps.text: Check the motor order and spin direction, and set where the flight controller and the GPS sit on the drawing of the aircraft. Test the motors with the propellers removed.

steps.label: Calibration
steps.title: Orientation and calibration
steps.text: First set how the controller is turned on the aircraft. Then calibrate the gyro, the accelerometer and the compass, and level the horizon. A changed rotation needs a reboot and a new calibration.

steps.label: Radio
steps.title: Radio control
steps.text: Bind the transmitter, calibrate the sticks and assign the flight mode switch. Skip this if you fly without a transmitter.

steps.label: Safety
steps.title: Safety and failsafes
steps.text: Set what the aircraft does when the radio or the battery fails, and which checks must pass before it arms.

steps.label: Battery
steps.title: Battery and power
steps.text: Enter the cell count and the capacity so the remaining charge is honest.

steps.label: Finish
steps.title: Ready to fly?
steps.text: Here is what is done and what is still open.
